newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: New oil and gas minister named for Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: New oil and gas minister named for Turkmenistan.

text.p: Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov named Deputy Prime Minister Batyr Sardjaev new oil and gas minister of the Central Asian state, according to a decree published on Tuesday.

Sardjaev replaces Gochmurad Nazdzhanov who will now be supervising the construction of planned oil and gas pipelines to link gas-rich Turkmenistan with Pakistan via Afghanistan with the participation of U.S. oil major Unocal Corp.

At a televised government meeting late on Monday, Niyazov berated Nazdzhanov for shortcomings at the ministry and over work on a $1 billion rehabilitation on the Turkmenbashi oil refinery in the west of the country.
"All this time, all the work at the ministry has been centred on the sale of oil and gas -- nobody there took care of of increasing the potential of this strategic sector," said Niyazov.
It is uncertain how much real weight the republic's oil and gas ministers hold as Niyazov brooks no dissent in the nation of 3.8 million and regularly criticises and dismisses his ministers.
Niyazov is looking to increased sales of gas to western Europe -- he has said about 20 billion cubic metres (bcm) in 1997 -- to put the impoverished desert nation back on its feet.
The rest of this year's officially targeted 53 bcm will be exported to Ukraine and other ex-Soviet states.

Last month, Nazdzhanov said the country aimed in the long term to produce about 85 bcm but exports are at present totally reliant on Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom GAZP.RTS, whose pipelines are the only means for Turkmenistan to export its gas.
